bullets: ‘The Phantom slowly, gravely, silently approached’: three adverbs create dread.
‘shrouded in a deep black garment, which concealed its head, its face, its form, and left nothing of it visible save one outstretched hand’: Grim Reaper imagery.
It never speaks; Scrooge must interpret: ‘I fear you more than any spectre I have seen.’
Businessmen joke about the funeral and only go if lunch is provided: indifference.

Old Joe’s den: the charwoman, laundress and undertaker’s man sell the dead man’s bed-curtains, blankets and shirt: ‘He frightened every one away from him when he was alive, to profit us when he was dead!’
The body lies ‘plundered and bereft, unwatched, unwept, uncared for’.
A young couple in debt feel relief at the death: the only emotion his death causes is joy for his debtors.
The house is quiet; Peter reads from the Bible.
Mrs Cratchit’s eyes are weak from sewing by candlelight: hides tears.
The empty corner and the crutch without an owner.
Contrast: Tiny Tim is mourned with love; Scrooge with no one.
The churchyard ‘overrun by grass and weeds… fat with repleted appetite’: neglected, grotesque.
Scrooge reads his own name: EBENEZER SCROOGE.
‘Are these the shadows of the things that Will be, or are they shadows of things that May be, only?’
‘I will honour Christmas in my heart, and try to keep it all the year.’
The phantom shrinks into a bedpost: return to reality.

callouts.p: Fear is the final lesson: Dickens shows readers that a life without love ends without love, and that change is still possible.

exam.q: Explore how Dickens creates fear in this extract (Stave 4, the Phantom). (20 marks)
exam.tip: Gothic features: darkness, death, silence, the uncanny.

mistakes.r: He realises only at the grave: dramatic irony for the reader.
mistakes.w: Scrooge knows from the start that the dead man is him.

quotes.q: to profit us when he was dead!
shadows of things that May be, only?

summary: Stave 4 is the climax: the silent Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come shows a death no one mourns, thieves selling the dead man’s belongings, the Cratchits grieving for Tiny Tim, and finally Scrooge’s own neglected grave, which drives him to repent.
